helix-bridge.tag: A double spiral of steel across Marina Bay.
helix-bridge.desc: A 280-metre footbridge opened in April 2010, its DNA-like double spiral of steel carrying the bayfront promenade to Marina Bay Sands. LEDs light its strands after dark.
helix-bridge.title: Helix Bridge: Marina Bay's Double-Spiral Footbridge
helix-bridge.meta: The Helix Bridge, a 280 m double-spiral steel footbridge opened in 2010, links the Marina Bay promenade to Marina Bay Sands. When to walk it and what to see.
helix-bridge.lead: Its steel strands twisted like DNA and lit by LEDs after dark, the Helix Bridge carries the Marina Bay promenade to the ArtScience end of Marina Bay Sands.
body: The Helix Bridge is a 280-metre footbridge, opened in April 2010, and one link in the promenade that runs around Marina Bay from Merlion Park past the Esplanade to Marina Bay Sands. Arup, Cox Group and Singapore's Architects 61 designed its double spiral of steel, which recalls the structure of DNA. After dark, LEDs light up its strands. Like the rest of the bay, it is best seen on foot.

Walk it at dusk, when the bridge glows and the towers of Raffles Place light up across the water. On the far side, Spectra, a free 15-minute show of fountains, light and mist, plays from the Event Plaza at Marina Bay Sands at 8pm and 9pm from Sunday to Thursday, and at 8pm, 9pm and 10pm on Fridays and Saturdays.

victoria-theatre.tag: Colonial theatre and concert hall on the river.
victoria-theatre.desc: The 1862 Town Hall and the 1905 Victoria Memorial Hall, joined by a 54-metre clock tower at Empress Place. The pair is a National Monument and home of the Singapore Symphony Orchestra.
victoria-theatre.title: Victoria Theatre and Concert Hall: Singapore's Civic Stage
victoria-theatre.meta: Victoria Theatre and Concert Hall at Empress Place: the 1862 Town Hall, the 1905 memorial hall, the 54 m clock tower, the Raffles statue and the SSO's home.
victoria-theatre.lead: Two halls and a 54-metre clock tower at Empress Place make up Victoria Theatre and Concert Hall, home of the Singapore Symphony Orchestra.
body: The theatre began life as the Town Hall, completed in 1862 at Empress Place, where the Singapore River curls past towards the bay. The concert hall followed in 1905 as the Victoria Memorial Hall, with a 54-metre clock tower rising between the two buildings. Both were upgraded from 2010 to 2014, and the pair, a National Monument since 1992, is home to the Singapore Symphony Orchestra.

Outside stands the bronze statue of Raffles, erected on the Padang in 1887 and moved here in 1919. The Asian Civilisations Museum is its neighbour at Empress Place, and the old City Hall and the Padang, where much of Singapore's history was decided, are within a few hundred metres. Walk the area in the morning, then shelter from the afternoon heat in a gallery.

Theatre 1862 (as the Town Hall); concert hall 1905

universal-studios.desc: Southeast Asia's first and only Universal Studios park, at Resorts World Sentosa: seven themed zones, including Minion Land, opened in February 2025, with Battlestar Galactica and Transformers as headline rides.
universal-studios.title: Universal Studios Singapore: Seven Zones on Sentosa
universal-studios.meta: Universal Studios Singapore at Resorts World Sentosa: its seven zones, headline rides, Minion Land, ticket prices from S$76 and tips for beating the queues.
universal-studios.lead: Southeast Asia's first and only Universal Studios park fits seven themed zones into a single day at Resorts World Sentosa.
body: Universal Studios Singapore opened on 18 March 2010, with a grand opening on 28 May 2011. Its seven zones are Hollywood, New York, Sci-Fi City, Ancient Egypt, The Lost World, Far Far Away and Minion Land, the newest, opened in February 2025. Battlestar Galactica and Transformers are the headline rides, and a Universal Express pass lets you skip the regular queues for a fee.

Next door, Adventure Cove Waterpark has a lazy river through 14 themed zones, tube slides and Rainbow Reef, for snorkelling among 20,000 reef animals. To get there, take the MRT to HarbourFront and ride the Sentosa Express from VivoCity to Resorts World station, paying the S$4 island admission as you board, or walk in free along the Sentosa Boardwalk.

siloso-beach.tag: Sentosa's liveliest beach, facing the ships.
siloso-beach.desc: The liveliest of Sentosa's three beaches, at the island's western end, with beach bars, watersports and a view of ships at anchor in the Singapore Strait. Stay for sunset and the Wings of Time show.
siloso-beach.title: Siloso Beach: Sentosa's Liveliest Stretch of Sand
siloso-beach.meta: Siloso Beach on Sentosa: beach bars, paddleboards and water jetpacks, sunset after Fort Siloso and the nightly Wings of Time show. Getting there and costs.
siloso-beach.lead: On Siloso Beach, Sentosa's liveliest, the horizon is never empty: every sunset is framed by the tankers anchored in the Singapore Strait.
body: Sentosa's beaches face the Singapore Strait, so the view is of ships at anchor rather than open sea. The island's name means tranquillity in Malay, but Siloso, in the west, is the liveliest of the three, with beach bars and watersports; Ola Beach Club rents paddleboards and water jetpacks. Palawan Beach suits families better, and Tanjong Beach, at the eastern end, is the quietest.

Fort Siloso is at Siloso Point, also in the west, so the two make a natural pair: explore the tunnels and gun emplacements in the afternoon, then come down for sunset. After dark, Wings of Time plays 20 minutes of fountains, lasers and fireworks on the beach, nightly at 7.40pm and 8.40pm. Public drinking is banned everywhere from 10.30pm to 7am, beaches included.

fort-siloso.tag: Coastal guns, tunnels and the story of 1942.
fort-siloso.desc: A coastal fort at Sentosa's western tip, built in the early 1880s, whose guns turned inland in February 1942. Tunnels, gun emplacements and the Surrender Chambers tell the story, and entry is free.
fort-siloso.title: Fort Siloso: Sentosa's Second World War Coastal Fort
fort-siloso.meta: Fort Siloso on Sentosa, a free coastal fort from the 1880s: tunnels, gun emplacements, the Surrender Chambers and the 11-storey Skywalk. Hours and tips.
fort-siloso.lead: At Siloso Point, guns built to guard Singapore's port were turned 180 degrees inland in February 1942 to fire on the advancing Japanese.
body: The British fortified the island, then called Pulau Blakang Mati, to guard the harbour. Work on Fort Siloso began in 1874, and the fort was built in the early 1880s, one of three guarding the port. In February 1942 its guns were turned 180 degrees inland to fire on Japanese positions, and during the Occupation that followed the fort held prisoners of war. It is now Singapore's 74th National Monument.

Tunnels and gun emplacements survive, and the Surrender Chambers, six interactive zones on the years 1942 to 1945, tell the story of the fall and the Occupation. The free Fort Siloso Skywalk climbs 11 storeys and is open from 9am to 7pm. Allow the afternoon, and finish with sunset on Siloso Beach below.
facts: Siloso Point, western Sentosa; the free Fort Siloso Skywalk climbs 11 storeys (daily 9am–7pm)

singapore-oceanarium.desc: The successor to the S.E.A. Aquarium at Resorts World Sentosa, opened in July 2025 at three times the size, where manta rays and zebra sharks glide past a 36-metre-wide Open Ocean panel.
singapore-oceanarium.title: Singapore Oceanarium: Sentosa's Rebuilt Aquarium
singapore-oceanarium.meta: The Singapore Oceanarium at Resorts World Sentosa, opened July 2025: the Open Ocean habitat, six themed zones, ticket prices from S$55 and evening entry.
singapore-oceanarium.lead: Rebuilt at three times the size of the old S.E.A. Aquarium, the Singapore Oceanarium opened in July 2025 with a window on the open ocean 36 metres wide.
body: The Singapore Oceanarium opened at Resorts World Sentosa on 23 July 2025, replacing the former S.E.A. Aquarium and rebuilt at three times its size across six themed zones. The route leads past a jellyfish kreisel and a life-sized whale fall to the Open Ocean habitat, where reef manta rays and zebra sharks glide behind a viewing panel 36 metres wide.

In the Spirit of Exploration zone stands a replica of the Jewel of Muscat, a ninth-century Arabian dhow. Entry is by timed ticket, and an evening ticket admits from 4pm. Under cover and out of the sun, the Oceanarium is a good choice for the hottest hours of a Sentosa day, between the beaches and Fort Siloso.

night-safari.tag: The world's first nocturnal wildlife park.
night-safari.desc: The world's first nocturnal wildlife park, opened in 1994 in the Mandai Wildlife Reserve, where more than 900 nocturnal animals are seen by tram and on walking trails. Open nightly from 6pm.
night-safari.title: Night Safari Singapore: The First Nocturnal Wildlife Park
night-safari.meta: Night Safari at Mandai, the world's first nocturnal wildlife park: tram and walking trails, opening hours, tourist prices, the Khatib shuttle and taxi tips.
night-safari.lead: When the sun goes down over Mandai, the Night Safari opens its gates on more than 900 nocturnal animals, seen from a tram and along forest trails.
body: The Night Safari opened on 3 May 1994, with an official opening on 26 May, as the world's first nocturnal wildlife park. Its 35 hectares in the Mandai Wildlife Reserve are home to more than 900 nocturnal animals. Ride the Safari Adventure Tram, with English audio commentary, then walk the Tasmanian Devil, Pangolin, Leopard and East Lodge trails; the trails and tram start from 7pm.

The park opens at 6pm, with last entry at 11.15pm, so it pairs well with an afternoon at Singapore Zoo or Bird Paradise in the same reserve. The M2 Khatib Shuttle runs from Khatib MRT every 15 to 20 minutes (S$2.50 one way, contactless payment only). Book ahead, arrive early in the evening and allow several hours.

bird-paradise.desc: Mandai's bird park, which it calls Asia's largest: walk-through aviaries full of free-flying birds, with a tram or shuttle included in admission. Pair it with the Night Safari for a full Mandai day.
bird-paradise.title: Bird Paradise Singapore: Mandai's Walk-Through Aviaries
bird-paradise.meta: Bird Paradise at Mandai, billed as Asia's largest bird park: walk-through aviaries, opening hours, tourist prices, combined passes and the Khatib shuttle.
bird-paradise.lead: At Bird Paradise, in the Mandai Wildlife Reserve, you walk inside the aviaries themselves, among birds flying free around you.
body: Bird Paradise is one of six attractions in the Mandai Wildlife Reserve, alongside Singapore Zoo, the Night Safari, River Wonders, Rainforest Wild Adventure and the indoor Exploria. The reserve lies on the northern edge of the Central Catchment's forests, and Mandai calls this Asia's largest bird park. Its walk-through aviaries are full of free-flying birds, and a tram or shuttle, included in admission, helps you get around the park.

It is open daily from 9am to 6pm, with last entry at 5pm, which makes it a natural afternoon before the Night Safari opens at 6pm; a 2 Attractions Destination Pass covers both in one day. The M2 Khatib Shuttle runs from Khatib MRT, and the free M1 East-West Shuttle links the two halves of the reserve.

tekka-centre.tag: Biryani and tandoor naan in Little India.
tekka-centre.desc: Little India's market and hawker centre on Buffalo Road, heir to the Kandang Kerbau Market of 1915, with many halal and vegetarian stalls. Come for biryani and tandoor naan.
tekka-centre.title: Tekka Centre: Biryani and Naan in Little India
tekka-centre.meta: Tekka Centre in Little India, heir to the 1915 Kandang Kerbau Market: biryani, tandoor naan, Bib Gourmand Delhi Lahori, history and how to get there.
tekka-centre.lead: Across the road from Little India MRT, Tekka Centre carries on a market tradition that began here in 1915, and its hawker stalls are known above all for biryani.
body: The original Kandang Kerbau Market, named after the old cattle district whose name means buffalo enclosure, opened in the first week of August 1915 where Serangoon Road meets Bukit Timah Road. Stallholders moved into the new complex across the road on 3 May 1981. It was called Zhujiao Centre from November 1981, under the Speak Mandarin Campaign, and became Tekka Centre in 2000.

The hawker centre has many halal and vegetarian stalls and is known for biryani. Try Delhi Lahori (#01-266), which holds a Bib Gourmand, for tandoor naan and kebabs, and look out for Malay dishes too. Come early in the morning, then walk on along Serangoon Road to the Sri Veeramakaliamman Temple.

Biryani, naan and kebabs, Malay dishes

mustafa-centre.tag: Little India's store that never closes.
mustafa-centre.desc: A sprawling discount department store in Little India, selling everything from electronics and gold to spices, saris and suitcases, and open 24 hours a day again since 6 September 2024.
mustafa-centre.title: Mustafa Centre: Little India's 24-Hour Department Store
mustafa-centre.meta: Mustafa Centre in Little India, the 24-hour discount department store: what to buy, from spices and gold to electronics, its history and the best time to go.
mustafa-centre.lead: At three in the morning, Mustafa's aisles still hum with shoppers buying saris, suitcases and saffron.
body: No shop in Singapore has a stronger legend. Mustafa grew from handkerchiefs sold beside a family food shop in 1971 into a garment shop, then a row of shophouses converted into a department store; by 1995 it was known as Mustafa Centre. In 2003 it became the first local department store to open 24 hours a day. Hours were cut during the pandemic, and round-the-clock trading resumed on 6 September 2024.

Its reputation is for selling just about everything: diamonds and watches, cameras and electronics, appliances and luggage, cheap clothing and sari fabrics, skincare, confectionery and fresh food, piled high across a warren of floors, with a supermarket too. Come for spices, Indian sweets, gold and a suitcase for the extra shopping; vacuum-packed spice blends travel well.
facts: Late at night, when the aisles are quietest

bugis-street.tag: A notorious night spot, reborn as a market.
bugis-street.desc: Once a notorious night spot for servicemen and sailors, Bugis Street was demolished in 1985 and recreated in the late 1980s as a pedestrianised shopping street opposite Bugis Junction.
bugis-street.title: Bugis Street: From Night-Time Legend to Market Street
bugis-street.meta: Bugis Street, the 1950s night spot of open-air food stalls and drag cabaret, demolished in 1985 and reborn as a pedestrianised shopping street by Bugis MRT.
bugis-street.lead: From the 1950s, Bugis Street was famous among soldiers and sailors for its open-air food stalls and its nightly parade of drag queens and trans women.
body: In the 1950s and 1960s the original Bugis Street was a notorious night spot, drawing servicemen and sailors to its open-air food stalls and to a nightly cabaret of drag queens and trans women. Its shophouses were demolished in October 1985 for redevelopment and the building of the MRT. A new Bugis Street was recreated in the late 1980s, opposite the original site, between Victoria and Queen Streets.

Today the recreated street is a pedestrianised shopping street on Victoria Street, opposite Bugis Junction and served by Bugis MRT. Kampong Glam is an easy walk away: Masjid Sultan, the textile shops of Arab Street and Haji Lane, reputedly Singapore's narrowest street, now packed with independent boutiques, bars and wall murals.

emerald-hill.tag: Peranakan terraces just off Orchard Road.
emerald-hill.desc: A conservation area of Peranakan terrace houses just off Orchard Road near Somerset MRT, with glazed tiles, bird-and-flower panels and pintu pagar swing doors. Allow about 30 minutes.
emerald-hill.title: Emerald Hill: Peranakan Terraces off Orchard Road
emerald-hill.meta: Emerald Hill, a 1989 conservation area of Peranakan terraces off Orchard Road: its nutmeg-orchard history, shophouse details and the best time to walk it.
emerald-hill.lead: A few steps from the malls of Orchard Road, Emerald Hill keeps a street of ornate terrace houses that were home to Peranakan families by the 1930s.
body: A former nutmeg orchard, Emerald Hill was bought in 1900 by Seah Eng Kiat and Seah Boon Kang, who sold it in plots for terraces and shophouses. By the 1930s many of the houses were home to Peranakan families. The street was gazetted as a conservation area in 1989, and it is a stop on the National Heritage Board's Orchard Heritage Trail.

The façades are worth slowing down for. Neoclassical columns mix with glazed tiles, bird-and-flower panels and pintu pagar, the half-height swing doors that let air in and kept eyes out. These are private homes, so admire them from the street. Allow about 30 minutes, and walk up from Orchard Road.
facts: Free (public street; the houses are private)
emerald-hill.tip: Walk up from Orchard Road in the morning, before the bars at the bottom open.

changi-chapel-museum.desc: The National Heritage Board's museum of the Allied prisoners of war and civilians interned at Changi during the Japanese Occupation, built around an open-sided replica of a prisoners' chapel.
changi-chapel-museum.title: Changi Chapel and Museum: Singapore's POW Story
changi-chapel-museum.meta: Changi Chapel and Museum tells the story of prisoners of war interned at Changi in WWII: the replica chapel, the galleries, opening hours, prices and buses.
changi-chapel-museum.lead: At the heart of the Changi Chapel and Museum stands an open-sided chapel, modelled on one of the many churches prisoners of war built during their internment.
body: During the Japanese Occupation, Allied prisoners of war and civilians were interned in the Changi Prison camp. The Changi Chapel and Museum, run by the National Heritage Board, tells their story through personal objects, art and testimony, in galleries on life as prisoners of war, resilience in adversity and the legacies of internment. When Singapore surrendered in February 1942, tens of thousands of British, Indian, Australian and local troops became prisoners of war.

At the centre stands an open-sided chapel modelled on St George's Church, one of the many churches the prisoners built in Changi. Allow time for the personal stories in the galleries; they suit older children with some context. Only cashless payment is accepted, and a family package of S$27 covers up to five people, with a maximum of three adults.
facts: Upper Changi MRT (Downtown Line, DT34), then bus 2; or bus 2 or 29 to the Changi Chapel Museum stop
Tue–Sun 9.30am–5.30pm; last admission 5pm; closed Mondays except public holidays
Tourists: adult S$9, concession S$7, 6 and under free; cashless only

kranji-war-memorial.tag: Commonwealth war graves in the north.
kranji-war-memorial.desc: The Commonwealth war cemetery at Kranji, where 4,461 graves lead up to the Singapore Memorial and its 24,346 names of the missing with no known grave. A short walk from Kranji MRT.
kranji-war-memorial.title: Kranji War Memorial: Singapore's Commonwealth War Graves
kranji-war-memorial.meta: Kranji War Cemetery and the Singapore Memorial: 4,461 war graves and 24,346 names of the missing, plus the State Cemetery. Opening hours, MRT and etiquette.
kranji-war-memorial.lead: Rows of white headstones lead up to the Singapore Memorial at Kranji, which records the names of 24,346 soldiers and airmen who have no known grave.
body: Kranji War Cemetery, at 9 Woodlands Road about 22 km from the city, holds 4,461 Commonwealth war burials. The graves lead up to the Singapore Memorial, which records the names of 24,346 soldiers and airmen who died in the Malaya and Indonesia campaigns or in captivity and have no known grave. It is the place in the north to see Singapore's wartime history.

The attack on Singapore came overland, down the Malay Peninsula: Japanese troops landed across the Strait of Johor on 8 February 1942, and a week later, on 15 February, Lieutenant-General Arthur Percival surrendered; tens of thousands of British, Indian, Australian and local troops became prisoners of war. Beside the war cemetery, the Kranji State Cemetery holds the graves of presidents Yusof bin Ishak and Benjamin Sheares.
facts: Kranji MRT (North-South Line), 10–15 minutes' walk; 9 Woodlands Road

henderson-waves.desc: Singapore's highest pedestrian bridge, 36 metres above Henderson Road, linking Mount Faber and Telok Blangah Hill on the Southern Ridges. Its curved ribs form shaded alcoves looking over the treetops.
henderson-waves.title: Henderson Waves: Singapore's Highest Footbridge
henderson-waves.meta: Henderson Waves, Singapore's highest pedestrian bridge, 36 m above Henderson Road on the Southern Ridges: its design, the walk, the views and when to go.
henderson-waves.lead: Thirty-six metres above Henderson Road, the deck of Henderson Waves rolls between Mount Faber and Telok Blangah Hill like a wave about to break.
body: Henderson Waves is the highest pedestrian bridge in Singapore, 274 metres long and 8 metres wide, standing 36 metres above Henderson Road. Seven curved ribs rise above and below the deck in a rolling wave, forming shaded alcoves where walkers pause to look over the treetops towards the harbour. With Alexandra Arch, it was completed in 2008 and officially opened by Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong on 10 May that year.

The bridge is the centrepiece of the Southern Ridges, a 10 km chain of hills from Mount Faber through Telok Blangah Hill and HortPark to Kent Ridge Park. The 1.3 km Forest Walk links it to Alexandra Arch. The full walk is long, hilly and partly exposed, so carry water, wear a hat and shelter quickly if lightning threatens.
facts: Southern Ridges, between Mount Faber and Telok Blangah Hill
Late afternoon into dusk, when the heat eases
henderson-waves.tip: Walk the Ridges west to east, then ride the cable car down from Mount Faber to Sentosa.

singapore-cable-car.tag: Gondolas from Mount Faber to Sentosa.
singapore-cable-car.desc: Gondolas swing from Mount Faber through HarbourFront to Sentosa, with a separate Sentosa Line across the island. Only round-trip or unlimited tickets are sold; a Sky Pass costs S$35 for adults.
singapore-cable-car.title: Singapore Cable Car: Mount Faber to Sentosa
singapore-cable-car.meta: Ride the Singapore Cable Car from Mount Faber via HarbourFront to Sentosa: the two lines, Sky Pass prices, opening hours, last boarding and Faber Point.
singapore-cable-car.lead: The Singapore Cable Car swings out from Mount Faber, 105 metres above sea level, through HarbourFront and on to Sentosa.
body: The Mount Faber Line runs from Mount Faber, the eastern anchor of the Southern Ridges, through HarbourFront to Sentosa, and a separate Sentosa Line links Siloso Point, Imbiah Lookout and Sensoryscape on the island. It is one of the ways onto Sentosa, alongside the Sentosa Express and the free Boardwalk. Only round-trip or unlimited tickets are sold: the Cable Car Sky Pass costs S$35 for adults and S$25 for children, round trip.

At the top, restaurants and a bar at Mount Faber Peak face the harbour and skyline, and Faber Point is a circular lookout with copper-tooled murals of Singapore's history and a Merlion statue. The best way to arrive is on foot: walk the Southern Ridges west to east, across Henderson Waves, then ride the cable car down to Sentosa.

Sky Pass round trip: adult S$35, child S$25

kusu-island.tag: Tortoise legend, temple and hilltop shrines.
kusu-island.desc: A small island about 5.6 km south of Singapore whose name means tortoise in Hokkien, with the Da Bo Gong temple and three Malay kramats up 152 steps. Ferries leave from Marina South Pier.
kusu-island.title: Kusu Island: Temple and Shrines on Tortoise Island
kusu-island.meta: Kusu Island, Singapore's Tortoise Island: the Da Bo Gong temple, three hilltop kramats, the ninth-month pilgrimage and ferries from Marina South Pier.
kusu-island.lead: Legend says a magical tortoise became Kusu Island to save two shipwrecked sailors, and pilgrims still cross to its temple and shrines every ninth lunar month.
body: Kusu means tortoise in Hokkien, and the island's legend tells of a magical tortoise that turned itself into land to save two shipwrecked sailors. Devotees pray at the Da Bo Gong temple, built in 1923, and on a hillock above, up 152 steps, three Malay kramats honour the 19th-century holy man Syed Abdul Rahman, his mother and his sister. Pilgrims come every ninth lunar month.

Ferries leave from Marina South Pier and loop to Lazarus, then Kusu, and back; return tickets start from S$15. A ticket allows one hop from St John's or Lazarus on to Kusu, but there is no ferry from Kusu back to the other islands, so visit St John's first. Overnight stays and pets are not permitted, and you should take your rubbish home.

kusu-island.tip: On weekdays the last ferry leaves Kusu at 4.15pm; weekend queues build, so avoid arriving after 3pm.

rail-corridor.tag: A 24 km green trail on the old railway.
rail-corridor.desc: The old line from the Malay Peninsula, returned to Singapore in 2011 and reborn as a 24 km green route from Woodlands to Tanjong Pagar, with Bukit Timah Railway Station on its central stretch.
rail-corridor.title: Rail Corridor: Walking Singapore's Old Railway Line
rail-corridor.meta: Walk the Rail Corridor, Singapore's 24 km green route along the old railway from Woodlands to Tanjong Pagar, via the restored Bukit Timah Railway Station.
rail-corridor.lead: Trains from the Malay Peninsula once ran through the heart of Singapore; their old line is now a 24 km green corridor from Woodlands to Tanjong Pagar.
body: When the railway land returned to Singapore in 2011, the line became the Rail Corridor, a 24 km ecological route from Woodlands to Tanjong Pagar. South of Rifle Range Road the trail is paved; north towards Kranji it turns to grass and gravel, a rustic stretch opened as Rail Corridor (North) in February 2023. The trail is flat, which makes it a good walk with children.

A good place to start is Bukit Timah Railway Station, built in 1932 and one of two surviving railway stations in Singapore. It reopened as a heritage gallery and community node on 1 July 2022, with restored track-switching levers, the old ticket booth and replica wagons, and the neighbouring Railway Staff Quarters house the 1932 Story Café.

The corridor is open 24/7 but unlit, to protect nocturnal wildlife, so leave by nightfall or carry a torch. Since 9 March 2026 the southern section between the Henderson Road and Spooner Road accesses has been closed for trail works; check railcorridor.nparks.gov.sg for notices.
facts: King Albert Park MRT (Exit A), about 5 minutes' walk to Bukit Timah Railway Station
rail-corridor.tip: From Bukit Timah Railway Station, walk south on the paved trail, or north for the wilder grass-and-gravel stretch.
